title: Studies show that mentoring can also benefit the mentors decades after experiences
summary_en: Mary Fry, professor of educational psychology at KU, has co-written two studies that examined mentoring programs. One found that the Strong Girls program benefited those providing the guidance to young girls 10 years after their experience, and another found “sideways mentoring” among peers helped scholars for as long as 20 years.
title_cn: Studies show that mentoring can also benefit the mentors decades after experiences

title: Research could lead to cheaper, better testing for ‘forever chemicals’ in US drinking water
summary_en: A new investigation from the University of Kansas improves detection of PFAS, a family of so-called “forever chemicals” in drinking water supplies. The method, which can measure such trace pollution levels of PFAS in water more quickly and inexpensively than current techniques, recently was published in the open-source journal PLOS Water.
title_cn: Research could lead to cheaper, better testing for ‘forever chemicals’ in US drinking water

title: KU exhibition explores global impact of sports design ahead of 2026 World Cup
summary_en: The University of Kansas School of Architecture & Design will present “Shaping the Future of Football,” an exhibition in Kansas City highlighting the region’s global role in sports architecture. Featuring World Cup stadium models, student design work and emerging technologies, the show explores how architecture, data and design are transforming the future of the game.
title_cn: KU exhibition explores global impact of sports design ahead of 2026 World Cup

title: American Constitution Society honors KU Law student and chapter with national recognition
summary_en: The American Constitution Society has recognized the University of Kansas School of Law and one of its student leaders with national honors for leadership and programming.
title_cn: American Constitution Society honors KU Law student and chapter with national recognition

title: University of Kansas launches Center for Workplace Excellence to empower organizations across Kansas City
summary_en: The Center for Workplace Excellence supports career development in the Greater Kansas City area, helping businesses and nonprofit organizations strengthen workforce skills, improve organizational effectiveness and navigate today’s rapidly changing workplace environment.
title_cn: University of Kansas launches Center for Workplace Excellence to empower organizations across Kansas City

title: KU Student Affairs announces return of Homecoming Parade
summary_en: The first University of Kansas Homecoming parade in seven years will take place Oct. 23, part of the 2026 Homecoming events. The parade will be led by Student Affairs in partnership with KU Alumni, Kansas Athletics Inc. and Jayhawk Community Partners.
title_cn: KU Student Affairs announces return of Homecoming Parade

title: Kansas science teachers to take part in immersive program at KU Field Station
summary_en: Ten secondary school science teachers from Kansas will converge this week at the University of Kansas Field Station, just north of Lawrence. They’ll take part in the Ecosystems of Kansas Summer Institute, an annual immersive program that gives secondary educators the chance to work with KU scientists to explore resources and gain new ideas for their classrooms.
title_cn: Kansas science teachers to take part in immersive program at KU Field Station

title: Love of language and libraries leads KU graduate to Rubinstein/Mason scholarship
summary_en: What started as a fondness for libraries and a curiosity about Korean hangul — the writing system and alphabet used for Korean language — has grown into a calling. University of Kansas graduate Daphne Tibbetts has been selected as the recipient of the 2026 Rubinstein/Mason Award to support graduate study in library science, with her sights set on becoming a Korean studies librarian.
title_cn: Love of language and libraries leads KU graduate to Rubinstein/Mason scholarship
